visuals.title: What to do with the cyst
Where cysts form
visuals.text: Dilated, fluid-filled terminal ductal-lobular units within the breast.

glossary.Benign: Not cancer; does not invade or spread.
glossary.Glandular tissue: The milk-producing lobules and ducts of the breast.
glossary.Connective tissue: Supporting fibrous tissue that holds the breast together.
glossary.Ducts: The tubes that carry milk from the lobules to the nipple.
glossary.Menstrual cycle: The roughly monthly hormone cycle of oestrogen and progesterone that leads to periods.
glossary.Breast pain: Also called mastalgia; often cyclical and linked to hormones.
glossary.Breastfeeding: Feeding a baby with breast milk; a galactocele can form after stopping.
glossary.Irregular mass: A lump with an uneven, poorly defined edge, a feature of cancer.
glossary.Urgent referral: Referral to be seen quickly, usually within two weeks, when cancer is suspected.
glossary.Symptomatic: Causing symptoms such as pain or a noticeable lump.
glossary.Reassurance: Explaining that the finding is harmless and needs no treatment.
glossary.Recurrence: The cyst or condition coming back after treatment.
glossary.Biopsy: Removal of a small piece of tissue for examination under the microscope.
glossary.Malignancy: A cancer: cells growing uncontrollably and able to invade or spread.
glossary.Menopause: The permanent end of periods as the ovaries stop making oestrogen.
glossary.Decompresses: Releases pressure by draining the fluid.
glossary.Solid elements: Non-fluid material in an aspirate, which raises suspicion of a tumour.
